skill.name: it-operations
skill.description: Guides IT infrastructure, observability, incident response, automation, backup, recovery, capacity planning, and ITIL service management.
skill.summary: Plan reliable operations, respond to incidents, and improve infrastructure practices with structured guidance.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most detections are documentation syntax, placeholders, or authorized operations examples. Confirmed risks include destructive automation, weak access controls, unsafe credentials, and privileged infrastructure changes.

remediation.issue: Autonomous remediation can delete files, restart services, and kill workloads.
remediation.suggestion: Require dry runs, strict allowlists, protected-process checks, rate limits, audit logs, and human approval before destructive actions.

remediation.issue: ChatOps handlers do not verify authorization for privileged actions.
remediation.suggestion: Enforce role checks, validated host allowlists, scoped service accounts, signed approvals, and complete requester audit records.

remediation.issue: Storage examples include formatting and removal commands without safety gates.
remediation.suggestion: Add prominent warnings, device identity checks, mounted-volume checks, backups, dry-run steps, and explicit confirmations.

remediation.issue: Examples use weak passwords and source-level credential placeholders.
remediation.suggestion: Use secret managers or workload identity, generate unique passwords, remove inline credentials, and document rotation procedures.

remediation.issue: Privileged installers download artifacts without integrity verification.
remediation.suggestion: Pin versions and verify checksums or signatures before installation. Use trusted package repositories where available.

remediation.issue: Remote access and firewall examples can expose management interfaces.
remediation.suggestion: Bind management services to trusted networks, require strong authentication, apply firewall rules atomically, and provide automatic rollback.

semantic_findings.title: Autonomous Process Termination
semantic_findings.description: The continuous remediation loop kills the largest non-whitelisted process when memory exceeds 90 percent. It lacks workload identity checks and operator approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code explicitly selects high-memory processes and calls kill every minute. Only three process names are excluded.

semantic_findings.title: Missing ChatOps Authorization
semantic_findings.description: Slack handlers restart services, target Ansible hosts, and approve deployments without checking caller roles or requiring a second approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The handlers accept command and action data, then perform privileged operations. No authorization or requester validation appears in the flow.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Default Credentials
semantic_findings.description: Copy-ready examples configure HAProxy statistics with password123 and Grafana with admin. These defaults can expose operational dashboards when deployed unchanged.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both examples contain explicit weak passwords in deployable configuration. Neither example requires secret injection or immediate rotation.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Firewall Replacement
semantic_findings.description: The firewall script flushes active rules before establishing replacements. An interruption can remove protections or disconnect remote administrators without rollback.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The sequence visibly flushes all filter and NAT chains before saving new rules. No atomic loader, rollback timer, or access check is included.

content.user_title: Strengthen IT Operations and Service Reliability
content.value_statement: IT teams need consistent methods for reliable services and incident response. This skill provides structured workflows, metrics, runbooks, automation guidance, and recovery practices.
actual_capabilities: Defines monitoring strategies using metrics, logs, traces, alerts, dashboards, SLIs, SLOs, and SLAs.
Provides incident severity models, response roles, communication templates, runbooks, and post-incident review structures.
Explains server, network, cloud, virtualization, storage, patching, and capacity planning workflows.
Compares automation approaches and provides examples for scripts, configuration management, CI pipelines, and ChatOps.
Covers backup selection, retention, recovery objectives, disaster recovery plans, restoration, and recovery testing.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples but does not inspect or operate infrastructure by itself.
Commands require environment-specific review, testing, authorization, and rollback planning before production use.
Tool versions, cloud settings, addresses, credentials, and thresholds are examples that require replacement.
Some examples contain unsafe defaults and destructive commands that require security remediation.

use_cases.title: Establish Operations Foundations
use_cases.description: Create monitoring, on-call, change, backup, and documentation practices for a growing technical organization.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Service Incidents
use_cases.description: Classify impact, assign response roles, communicate status, follow diagnostics, and prepare a blameless review.

use_cases.title: Improve Platform Reliability
use_cases.description: Evaluate alerts, capacity, toil, automation opportunities, recovery objectives, and infrastructure lifecycle practices.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Operations Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a weekly IT operations checklist for [systems]. Include monitoring, backups, access reviews, patching, and documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Incident Runbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a runbook for [incident]. Include severity, diagnostics, roles, communications, rollback, validation, and escalation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Monitoring Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Design monitoring for [service]. Define SLIs, SLOs, golden signals, alert thresholds, dashboards, and ownership.

prompt_templates.title: Assess an Automation Proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this automation plan: [plan]. Identify privileges, failure modes, approvals, safeguards, rollback, audit requirements, and measurable benefits.

output_examples.input: Create a P1 response plan for a customer-facing API outage.
output: Declare P1 and assign incident commander, operations lead, communications lead, and scribe.
Confirm impact, review recent changes, inspect dependencies, and prepare rollback.
Publish updates every 30 minutes and schedule a post-incident review.

output_examples.input: Recommend monitoring for a PostgreSQL service.
output: Track availability, query latency, connection saturation, replication lag, storage growth, and backup freshness.
Page on sustained availability or data-risk conditions. Create tickets for capacity trends.
Link every alert to an owned dashboard and tested runbook.

output_examples.input: Outline a quarterly disaster recovery exercise.
output: Confirm recovery objectives, owners, test scope, backups, dependencies, and communication channels.
Execute controlled failover, validate critical workflows, measure recovery, and return through an approved plan.
Record gaps, assign actions, and retest failed controls.

best_practices: Test commands in isolated environments and require approvals for privileged or destructive changes.
Define service ownership, measurable objectives, escalation paths, and tested rollback procedures.
Review alerts, runbooks, backups, access, capacity, and recovery results on a regular schedule.
anti_patterns: Do not copy example credentials, addresses, device names, or destructive commands into production.
Do not allow ChatOps or self-healing automation to act without authorization, boundaries, and audit logs.
Do not treat successful backups as proof of recovery without regular restoration tests.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to my infrastructure?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Connection and execution depend on tools, permissions, and actions available in your environment.

faq.question: Can I run the commands as written?
faq.answer: Review and adapt every command first. Several examples require privileged access and can modify services, accounts, networks, or storage.

faq.question: Which operations frameworks are covered?
faq.answer: The skill covers ITIL practices, site reliability concepts, observability, incident management, change management, and disaster recovery.

faq.question: Can it help create incident runbooks?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides severity models, roles, diagnostic structures, communication templates, escalation paths, recovery steps, and review formats.

faq.question: Does it support cloud and on-premises systems?
faq.answer: Yes. Examples cover Linux, Windows, networking, virtualization, AWS, Terraform, Kubernetes, configuration management, monitoring, and backup tools.

faq.question: How should teams use the automation examples safely?
faq.answer: Use isolated testing, least privilege, allowlists, approvals, dry runs, rate limits, audit logs, and verified rollback procedures.
